maria: quick dump — ran 6h perf sweep on continuous-batcher w/ mixed short(<=16) + long(>512) sequences. saw a 22% p95 latency regression when KV cache hit-rate drops below ~65% and kernel fallback to fp16->int8 path occurs. trace attached in GCS: gs://redwood-ci/perf/1718023456/batch-sweep.tar.gz

jason: ack — do you have the profile flamegraph? where's the time going, kernel launch vs memcpy vs queue wait?

maria: flamegraph shows two hotspots: (1) kernel selection glue code spending ~12% CPU due to repeated heuristic recalcs when batch composition shifts, (2) runaway microbatches causing GPU to fire lots of tiny kernels -> kernel-launch overhead increases. KV miss spikes correlate with microbatch churn.

kai: interesting. so when kv-hit falls, more decoding steps hit larger seqs -> batch heterogeneity increases? that would explain kernel mismatch.

sasha: can you paste the kernel selection log sample? want to see the rule that flips between aten_fp16 and int8_fused paths.

maria: pasted snippet: ```
[batch_id=2431] composition=[short:12,long:1024] selected_kernel=aten_fp16
[batch_id=2432] composition=[short:8,short:10] selected_kernel=int8_fused
[batch_id=2433] composition=[short:2,long:1024] fallback_to=aten_fp16 (latency_penalty=+18ms)
```

pradeep: ugh. two ideas: (A) add a hysteresis window to kernel selection so we don't flip for modest composition changes, (B) bias admission to prefer batching by length class for a short probation period.

jason: +1 for hysteresis. also we should adjust token-budget accounting so short requests can't steal token quota repeatedly causing long requests to be forced into new batches (that creates tiny kernels). propose token_budget_target per-worker = 2560 tokens / s as baseline; tune from there.

kai: can we make admission policy soft-first: if worker is near budget but batch has a long req, respond with soft-429 (Retry-After: 0.1) instead of immediate shed? that buys time to assemble better batch.

sasha: users care about p50, p95. soft-429 might increase p50 if clients back off. need telemetry. what's the perf regression delta if we apply a 100ms retry vs immediate accept?

maria: ran a micro-sim: 100ms retry on long requests reduced p95 by ~14% and overall GPU utilization improved slightly. but tail still bad when kv-hit < 50%.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of "kernel-hysteresis:v2" scheduled to eng-runtime-canary for 12:00 UTC 

pradeep: action items from my side: (1) implement kernel-selection hysteresis flag (threshold + decay window), (2) add length-class sticky admission for 200ms probation, (3) augment token-budget exporter with per-worker running average.

jason: I'll own the telemetry dashboards: add kv_hit vs p95 overlay and soft-429 incidence. Need the new metrics names: token_budget.available, admission.sticky_ratio, kernel.switch_count.

sasha: I'll run an A/B on soft-429 behavior with real clients (50% soft, 50% default) for 6h and collect p50/p95, retry loops, and user-visible error rates.

maria: summary: small code changes + canary tomorrow. expect 2-3% overall latency improvement if kv-hit stays >=70%. If kv-hit drops <50% we need fallback plan: preemptive admission to prioritize long tails (i.e., admit longs first or route to dedicated pool).

jason: noted. also add a lint/gate test to ensure kernel-selection doesn't oscillate rapidly — make switch_count per-1000batches < 0.05.

maria: thanks — leaving TODOs in the tracker: RH-1047 (hysteresis), RH-1048 (sticky-admit), RH-1049 (telemetry). ping me if you need traces. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
